evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Hasina's government because the reprisals were alleged against state actors and were triggered by the government's response to sanctions.

evidence.title: Bangladesh: Freedom on the Net 2022 Country Report
evidence.claim: Freedom House also says online mobilization remained more viable in 2022 than in prior years, indicating some residual civic space despite the broader crackdown.
evidence.locator: Key Developments bullet on online mobilization
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Same primary country report, but this is a distinct favorable claim about online organizing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level context rather than a ruler credit claim; it is a narrow counterpoint to the broader repression record.
contrary_evidence: This does not offset the report's broader finding that authorities continued to arrest critics and expand surveillance powers.

evidence.title: Bangladesh: Authorities must end repression of demonstrations
evidence.claim: Amnesty said the authorities were escalating a crackdown on demonstrations, with about 1,400 political activists arrested and more than 60 people injured in the 7 December Dhaka clashes, and called for an end to excessive force and impunity.
evidence.locator: Background section and the quoted regional director statement
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights-organization statement tied to a specific 2022 protest crackdown.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Bangladesh authorities under Hasina's government; the report is on state response, not isolated local misconduct.
contrary_evidence: The article relies on media reports for the casualty count, so the exact numbers remain partly contingent.

evidence.title: Bangladesh: Crackdown on Political Opposition
evidence.claim: HRW reported that since late August 2022 at least four people had died and hundreds had been injured in clashes involving police, BNP supporters, and ruling-party supporters, while police carried out mass arrests of opposition supporters and ruling-party affiliates appeared to enjoy impunity for attacks.
evidence.locator: Opening paragraphs and the Banani candlelight-vigil incident description
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous rights-monitor reporting with specific incident detail.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Hasina's government because it concerns police conduct and ruling-party-aligned impunity during opposition protests.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes that each side accused the other of instigating violence, so not every clash is exclusively state-caused.

evidence.title: Police-ruling party men are defendants in 47pc DSA cases
evidence.claim: A CGS-linked analysis cited by Prothom Alo said police and ruling-party actors were the plaintiffs or defendants in 47 percent of Digital Security Act cases, and that the law was being used heavily against journalists and critics.
evidence.locator: Opening paragraphs and the 'Misuse against journalists' section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting that cites a specific research organization and gives concrete case-pattern data.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Hasina's government because the DSA was used by police and ruling-party actors against critics and journalists.
contrary_evidence: This is a pattern report, not a court finding on every individual case.

evidence.title: Govt scraps Odhikar’s registration
evidence.claim: The government cancelled Odhikar's registration because it said the rights group had published misleading information about extrajudicial killings, disappearances and murders, despite a long-running renewal case.
evidence.locator: Lead paragraphs and the explanation of the NGO Affairs Bureau letter, lines 198-205 and 213-227
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting with direct documentary detail from the bureau letter.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Hasina's government because the cancellation was carried out by the NGO Affairs Bureau under the Prime Minister's Office.
contrary_evidence: The government framed the cancellation as a paperwork and compliance issue, not purely as retaliation.

evidence.title: Mr. Abdur Rouf Talukder Former Governor, Bangladesh Bank
evidence.claim: Abdur Rouf Talukder joined as the 12th governor of Bangladesh Bank on 12 July 2022 after a long finance-ministry career; the bio says he contributed to budget reform, macroeconomic management, and IT in public financial management.
evidence.locator: bio paragraphs identifying his appointment and prior roles
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official biography page from the central bank, with direct appointment and career details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect. The page does not show Sheikh Hasina ordering the appointment, but it documents the government-selected central-bank leadership available to her administration.
contrary_evidence: The same bio shows a senior finance-ministry insider, so it supports competence but also suggests closeness to the executive rather than institutional independence.

evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2021 Article IV Consultation with Bangladesh
evidence.claim: The IMF said Bangladesh entered the pandemic with macroeconomic stability, announced support packages worth Tk 1.9 trillion by curtailing non-priority spending, and had macro policies that kept inflation stable, debt-to-GDP low, and external buffers adequate.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IMF country assessment with concrete macro indicators and policy response description.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Hasina administration's economic policy, not to Hasina personally; the source evaluates government and central-bank actions.
contrary_evidence: The same report warns that FY22 inflation would rise to 5.9 percent and the current account deficit would widen, so it is not an unalloyed success story.

evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2021 Article IV Consultation with Bangladesh
evidence.claim: IMF directors urged Bangladesh to monitor inflation closely, normalize monetary policy, gradually increase exchange-rate flexibility, safeguard reserves, strengthen bank regulation and supervision, improve corporate governance, and address corruption.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IMF Board summary with explicit reform prescriptions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect. It reflects the policy environment and the government's available choices rather than a direct personal act by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The report also acknowledges the government's rapid pandemic response and fiscal prudence, so the record is mixed rather than purely negative.

evidence.title: IMF Staff Reaches Staff-Level Agreement with Bangladesh on the Extended Credit Facility/Extended Fund Facility and the Resilience and Sustainability Facility
evidence.claim: The IMF said the new program aimed to restore macroeconomic stability, protect the vulnerable, create fiscal space, contain inflation, modernize the monetary policy framework, strengthen the financial sector, improve the business climate, and build climate resilience.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF mission statement with detailed policy objectives and rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect, as a government-level reform program negotiated with the Hasina administration rather than a personal statement by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The same press release says the economy had been hit by a sharp widening of the current account deficit, rapid reserve decline, rising inflation, and slowing growth.

evidence.title: World Bank Helps Bangladesh Build Economic Resilience
evidence.claim: The World Bank said its $250 million financing would help Bangladesh build a stronger fiscal and financial sector, streamline the bank recovery framework, and support a legislative framework on payments to create a more efficient financial system.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank press release on a Bangladesh policy credit with specific reform content.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level policy action under the Hasina administration; the source does not isolate personal direction by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The financing was designed to address resilience gaps, which implies the existing fiscal and financial systems still needed strengthening.

evidence.title: Strong Trade Competitiveness, Financial Sector, and Well-functioning Cities are Critical for Sustained Growth in Bangladesh: World Bank
evidence.claim: The World Bank said Bangladesh needed a strong reform agenda to sustain growth, especially to address trade competitiveness erosion, financial-sector vulnerabilities, orderly urbanization, digital development, climate change, private-sector financing, and export diversification.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank country press release summarizing a country economic memorandum.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a country-level reform assessment under the Hasina administration, not a direct ruler statement.
contrary_evidence: The same piece credits Bangladesh with remarkable development progress and very fast growth over the previous decade.

evidence.title: World Bank-Funded Project Drives Public Procurement Reform in Bangladesh
evidence.claim: The e-GP portal brought public procurement online, cut procurement costs by about 7 percent, reduced tender time from 100 days to 57 days, processed 80 percent of public procurement expenditure in FY21, and improved integrity by reducing external influences and preserving audit trails.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank results page with concrete implementation and outcome metrics.
evidence.period_fit: retrospective but highly relevant to 2022 governance conditions
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level reform implementation under the Hasina administration; the result page does not prove personal oversight by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The need to strengthen procurement integrity implies prior corruption and influence risks were material.

evidence.title: National Budget Speech 2022-2023
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Bangladesh
evidence.claim: The FY2022-23 budget speech made inflation control, a competitive exchange rate, continued economic development, employment generation, and emergency support for low-income people explicit priorities, including a Tk 5,000 crore fund for shocks from natural disasters or other crises.
evidence.locator: Chapter Seven and the low-income support section, lines 894-901 and 1237-1242
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government budget speech with explicit policy priorities and allocations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect. The document is the finance minister's budget speech for the Hasina government; it reflects administration priorities, not a direct personal statement by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The speech is aspirational and does not itself prove successful execution.

evidence.title: National Budget Speech 2022-2023
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Bangladesh
evidence.claim: The budget allocated Tk 183,425 crore to social infrastructure, Tk 31,761 crore to primary and mass education, Tk 29,282 crore to health, Tk 44,690 crore to local government and rural development, and Tk 4,290 crore to women and children affairs; it also said social safety-net coverage had reached 29 percent of households and allocations had risen almost eight-fold since FY2008-09.
evidence.locator: Chapter Six and social-safety-net section, lines 1028-1033, 1799-1801, 5651-5654, 2403-2406, and 2515-2519
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget text with explicit sectoral allocations and social-protection targets.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect government policy under the Hasina administration; the speech itself is by the finance minister, not Hasina personally.
contrary_evidence: The speech reports planned rather than audited outcomes, so implementation remains to be verified.

evidence.title: CPI 2022: Disappointing global and Bangladesh performances
evidence.claim: TIB said Bangladesh scored 25 on the CPI 2022, ranked 147th, and that the lack of visible action over the previous decade and the growth of impunity and political influence over accountability institutions had worsened corruption control.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: National TI chapter summarizing the CPI results and providing Bangladesh-specific interpretation with concrete score/rank data.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level anti-corruption performance under the Hasina administration; the report does not isolate individual personal decisions.
contrary_evidence: TIB explicitly notes the government's repeated anti-corruption pledges, so the source mixes stated intent with poor implementation.

evidence.title: Household Expenditure Survey 2022: Families Spend 42% of Income on Food | BBS Report
evidence.claim: The HIES 2022 report found that families spent about 42 percent of monthly income on food and only Tk 923 on average was left as savings, indicating substantial household budget pressure.
evidence.locator: Sector-wise expenditure section and the opening paragraphs, lines 41-46 and 53-55
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reputable local reporting of the official BBS survey, but the underlying survey report is more authoritative than the news article.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level outcome under the Hasina administration; not direct proof of ruler action or omission.
contrary_evidence: The survey is a 2022 snapshot and does not by itself separate government policy from imported inflation or private consumption shocks.

evidence.title: Total labour force in the country is 73.41m
evidence.claim: The provisional Labour Force Survey 2022 said Bangladesh's total labour force reached 73.41 million and the unemployment rate fell to 3.6 percent from 4.2 percent in 2016-17.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official news service reporting BBS provisional survey results; useful for labor-market context but still one-step removed from the underlying report.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level outcome under the administration, not direct evidence of a specific Hasina policy choice.
contrary_evidence: The piece reports labor-force expansion more than job quality, so it does not settle underemployment or real-wage questions.

evidence.title: Bangladesh’s current account deficit widens as imports surge
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Bangladesh's current account deficit widened to 4.2 percent of GDP in FY22, foreign-exchange reserves fell below $40 billion, and the government sought IMF support after import costs surged and remittances fell.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting replicated by a major Bangladeshi outlet with concrete macro figures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects the Hasina government's macroeconomic position and response, not necessarily a personally directed policy error.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes Bangladesh had been one of the world's fastest-growing economies for years, so the 2022 deterioration sits against a strong prior trend.

evidence.title: Structural Reforms are Essential to Sustain Growth & Poverty Reduction in Bangladesh
evidence.claim: The World Bank said extreme poverty in Bangladesh had fallen to 5 percent in 2022 from 9 percent in 2016, with other wellbeing indicators such as infant mortality, stunting, electricity access, sanitation, and education also improving.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank feature summarizing 2022 poverty survey results and broader welfare trends.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Outcome-level evidence under the Hasina administration, not direct proof of a specific policy choice.
contrary_evidence: The same feature warns that growth sustainability now requires policy adjustments because of balance-of-payments pressure, rising inflation, and financial-sector vulnerabilities.

evidence.title: UNICEF: Children call for more government investment in education, health and protection
evidence.claim: Nine in ten Bangladeshi children said it was very important for government to spend more on education and health; over 85 percent prioritized more education spending to recover learning loss; over 65 percent prioritized more social workers; UNICEF also said child-sector investment had stagnated at around 15 percent of public expenditure.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct UNICEF press release with concrete survey findings and budget-related claims.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect. This reflects government policy priorities under the Hasina administration, not a personal statement by Sheikh Hasina.
contrary_evidence: This is a survey of preferences and budget concerns, so it does not prove that policy delivered the desired outcomes.

evidence.title: Government commits to strengthening the social services workforce for the protection of children
evidence.claim: The Government of Bangladesh said it would recruit 6,000 new social workers, increasing the workforce from 3,000 to 9,000, and the symposium was opened by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who said child protection services should be available at community level.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF report of a government commitment, with direct quote from the Prime Minister.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct enough for attribution of government commitment; the source does not prove that Hasina personally designed the staffing plan, but it does place the commitment in her public presence and message.
contrary_evidence: The same page says 45 million children under 15 were regularly subjected to physical and psychological violence at home and that Bangladesh had only 3,000 social workers before the expansion.

evidence.title: Learning from the education sector's COVID-19 response to prepare for future emergencies (Bangladesh)
evidence.claim: Bangladesh's 20-month COVID-19 school closures led the Ministry of Education to create a remote learning strategy using television, radio, and digital lessons, plus printed materials that supported 150,933 children from marginalized groups in 842 schools.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF publication with specific implementation detail and target-group coverage numbers.
evidence.period_fit: retrospective on the 2022 education recovery context
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect. This is a ministry-led response under the Hasina administration rather than a personal directive by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The strategy was a response to long school closures, so it shows remediation of damage as much as proactive gain.

evidence.title: WHO Bangladesh Country Cooperation Strategy: 2020-2025
evidence.claim: WHO said Bangladesh had made remarkable socioeconomic progress, including poverty reduction, improvements in women's education, rising life expectancy, and better population health indicators such as under-five mortality reduction, while also noting progress in reducing maternal, infant, and child deaths, malnutrition, and increasing immunization coverage; the government prioritized people-centred accessible health systems focused on governance, health-system strengthening, and quality.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary WHO country strategy summarizing progress and government priorities in health systems.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level health policy under the Hasina administration, not a personal ruling act.
contrary_evidence: WHO also says the system still faced high out-of-pocket payments, inequitable access, weak quality of care, shortages of skilled providers, and widespread informal providers.

evidence.title: Bangladesh country strategic plan (2022-2026)
evidence.claim: WFP said Bangladesh was self-sufficient in rice, meat, and fish and on track to meet high-level targets for reduced stunting and wasting, but still faced a triple burden of malnutrition; its strategic outcomes aimed to ensure basic food and nutrition needs during crises and meet the nutrition needs of women, children, and vulnerable groups through strengthened national institutions and gender- and nutrition-sensitive social safety nets.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary WFP strategy document with explicit country objectives and vulnerability focus.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect. This is the government-aligned WFP strategy environment rather than a personal Hasina statement.
contrary_evidence: The same plan says the pandemic created a new group of poor and vulnerable Bangladeshis, especially in urban areas, and that Rohingya refugees remained highly food-insecure without assistance.

evidence.title: WFP Bangladesh - Assessments
evidence.claim: WFP said nearly one third of Bangladesh's population faced food insecurity and 20 percent lived below the national poverty line; since 2017 it had been providing food assistance and nutrition services in the Cox's Bazar Rohingya camps and surrounding community, along with life-skills training, disaster-risk-reduction activities, and engineering services.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary WFP overview page summarizing the country's vulnerability and program response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level context under the Hasina administration; the source does not attribute the conditions to one person specifically.
contrary_evidence: The page emphasizes significant economic growth, so the food-insecurity figures do not imply total policy failure but they do show major unmet need.

evidence.title: Over 1.5 million children at risk as devastating floods hit Bangladesh
evidence.claim: UNICEF said more than 1.5 million children were at increased risk from flooding in north-eastern Bangladesh and that it was on the ground with government and non-government partners to meet urgent safety, health, nutrition, clean-water, and education needs; UNICEF was also supporting the government flood response with water purification tablets, hygiene kits, therapeutic milk, learning kits, and social workers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF emergency response statement with concrete numbers and response actions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect government response context under the Hasina administration, not a personal act by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The same report shows the scale of harm: over four million people were affected, schools were submerged, and children were losing learning time.

evidence.title: Structural Reforms are Essential to Sustain Growth & Poverty Reduction in Bangladesh
evidence.claim: The World Bank said extreme poverty in Bangladesh fell to 5 percent in 2022 from 9 percent in 2016, and that other wellbeing measures also improved, including infant mortality, stunting, access to electricity, sanitary toilets, and education; rural areas saw faster poverty reduction than urban areas, though urban inequality widened.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank retrospective on 2022 poverty and wellbeing outcomes with explicit metrics.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Outcome-level evidence under the Hasina administration, not direct proof of a specific personal decision.
contrary_evidence: The same article says sustaining growth requires policy adjustments and notes balance-of-payments pressure, rising inflation, and financial-sector vulnerabilities.

evidence.title: Public Finance for Children
evidence.claim: UNICEF said Bangladesh's flagship Mother and Child Benefit Programme covered 1.25 million beneficiaries in 2022-23 and was planned to expand to 4 million by 2023-24 and 6 million by 2026; it also said the child budget share remained stagnant at 15.05 percent and identified low utilization and rushed end-of-year spending as implementation challenges.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF policy note with explicit program coverage, financing, and implementation critique.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect government policy under the Hasina administration; the note is not a personal directive by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The same note says child-budget shares were stagnant and implementation suffered from low utilization and rushed spending, so it is mixed rather than a clean success story.

evidence.title: Progress on breastfeeding in Bangladesh undermined by aggressive formula milk marketing - WHO, UNICEF
evidence.claim: The WHO/UNICEF report said 51 percent of surveyed parents and pregnant women had been targeted by formula-milk marketing; in Bangladesh, 65 percent of women exclusively breastfed up to five months and 98 percent wanted to breastfeed, yet the report called for stronger enforcement of Bangladesh's national code legislation and breastfeeding support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary WHO/UNICEF report with Bangladesh-specific data and a clear policy recommendation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly system-level rather than personal attribution; useful as evidence of regulatory gap under the Hasina administration.
contrary_evidence: The source shows strong breastfeeding intent among families, so the problem is partly regulatory and enforcement-related rather than simply behavioral.

evidence.title: UNICEF: New report details shocking deprivation of children living on the street
evidence.claim: The Survey on Street Children 2022 found that children living on the street in Bangladesh faced deprivation, extreme poverty, malnutrition, disease, illiteracy, and violence; UNICEF said the numbers could be in the millions and that it was working with the government as it invested in more social workers to help children leave the streets.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF release based on a 2022 survey with specific vulnerability and harm indicators.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect government context under the Hasina administration; the source does not isolate one decision-maker but does identify the need for state response.
contrary_evidence: The report is about severe unmet need, so it is mainly negative evidence even though it also notes government social-worker involvement.

evidence.title: Media in Bangladesh free to criticise my government: PM Hasina
evidence.claim: Hasina publicly said Bangladeshi media could say whatever they wished and that criticism remained free, while answering a question about the Digital Security Act.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report of a direct public statement by the ruler with clear date and context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct public statement by Sheikh Hasina about her own government's media environment.
contrary_evidence: HRW and Freedom House documented journalist arrests, self-censorship, and DSA-based pressure in the same period.

evidence.title: Free, fair polls held only during AL govt, PM Hasina tells BBC
evidence.claim: Hasina said free and fair elections had only happened under Awami League rule and told the BBC to judge disappearance allegations by how true they were.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous report of an interview statement by the ruler, with exact quoted claims and a dated interview context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct public statement by Sheikh Hasina about elections and disappearances during her tenure.
contrary_evidence: Freedom House and HRW described manipulated elections, pressure on critics, and unresolved disappearance allegations.

evidence.title: PM asks to give befitting reply to anti-Bangladesh propaganda
evidence.claim: Hasina urged supporters to counter what she called propaganda and described critics as spreading false and fabricated information about Bangladesh and her government.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official wire report of a direct ruler statement with clear date, but the claim is self-serving and needs corroboration by contrary evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct public statement by Sheikh Hasina; the claim concerns her own government and its critics.
contrary_evidence: Independent reporting in 2022 documented the government's retaliation against critics, activists, and rights groups.

evidence.title: AL government never violates human rights
evidence.claim: Hasina said the Awami League never violates human rights and instead protects rights.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous quotation reported in a wire summary; exact wording is recoverable from the snippet, though not from an open page fetch.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct public statement by Sheikh Hasina about her own party's conduct.
contrary_evidence: HRW, Freedom House, and UN-related reporting in 2022 documented arbitrary arrests, repression, and impunity.

evidence.title: Govt scraps Odhikar’s registration
evidence.claim: The government cancelled Odhikar's registration after the group documented disappearances and killings, and the letter said the organization spread misleading information that tarnished the state's image.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed contemporaneous reporting with a copy of the official letter and specific administrative action against a rights group.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The action was taken by a bureau under the government led by Hasina; it directly targeted a group documenting state abuses.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes Odhikar was one of the few groups systematically logging disappearances, so the government's rationale is contested.

evidence.title: Bangladesh Government Keeps Rewarding Rights Abusers
evidence.claim: HRW reported that Hasina rewarded sanctioned RAB and police officials with promotions and medals instead of accountability, and the government sent one sanctioned police chief to a UN event to bypass a US travel ban.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed contemporaneous NGO reporting that ties the action to named sanctioned officials and to Hasina's own awards and government decisions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Hasina and her government through awards, promotions, and delegation decisions involving sanctioned loyalists.
contrary_evidence: The government claimed business as usual and reform was unnecessary, which reinforces rather than weakens the abuse pattern.

evidence.title: Govt to send IGP Benazir to UN event
evidence.claim: Bangladesh decided to send police chief Benazir Ahmed to a UN summit even though the US had sanctioned him for human-rights violations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific, dated report of an official government decision involving a sanctioned official and public funds.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government action under Hasina's cabinet; it shows tolerance and validation of a sanctioned loyalist.
contrary_evidence: The article itself notes the US sanctions and the government's effort to work around them, which cuts against any claim of accountability.

evidence.title: Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2022 Country Report
evidence.claim: Freedom House said unqualified Awami League loyalists were alleged to be getting court positions, and that cases against ruling-party activists were regularly withdrawn for 'political consideration'.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Established country report with explicit claims about judicial politicization and preferential treatment for ruling-party actors.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant: it describes patronage and impunity patterns under the AL government led by Hasina, not a single personal act.
contrary_evidence: These are allegations and structural observations rather than a direct finding of Hasina's personal intent in one discrete case.

evidence.title: World Report 2022: Bangladesh
evidence.claim: HRW said the government used the Digital Security Act to harass and detain critics, targeted family members of diaspora journalists, denied disappearance findings, and reacted to spyware allegations by offering a peacekeeping explanation the UN rejected.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual country report with multiple specific mechanisms of concealment, retaliation, and official denial tied to Hasina's government.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The abuses are attributed to the Awami League-led government under Hasina; the report also records official denial and an implausible cover explanation from security officials.
contrary_evidence: The government's denials and the UN's rejection of the equipment explanation are themselves evidence against candor.

evidence.title: Bangladesh appoints Abdur Rouf Talukder as central bank governor
evidence.claim: The government appointed career finance secretary Abdur Rouf Talukder, who had decades of public-finance experience, as Bangladesh Bank governor.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Clear, dated appointment notice with a professional biography and no apparent controversy in the appointment itself.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Hasina's government made the appointment; this is a modest positive counterexample to a pure-cronyism narrative.
contrary_evidence: A single professional appointment does not show broader independence or honesty across the government.

evidence.title: ACC probes land allocation allegations involving Sheikh Hasina, family
evidence.claim: The Anti-Corruption Commission opened a probe alleging that Hasina, during her tenure as prime minister, misused authority to allocate six government plots to herself and close family members.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Later but specific investigative reporting tied to an official probe, with direct allegations about family benefit and misuse of authority.
evidence.period_fit: retrospective about conduct during Hasina's tenure; not a discrete 2022 event
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong family/office nexus: the allegations describe personal benefit to Hasina and relatives through government land allocation while she was in office.
contrary_evidence: This is an allegation/probe, not a final judicial finding, so it should be treated cautiously.

reasons.reason: Retrospective 2024 probe of alleged conduct during Hasina's tenure; usable only as corroborative context, not as target-period proof.

evidence.title: 8th Five Year Plan (English Version)
evidence.publisher: General Economics Division, Bangladesh Planning Commission
evidence.claim: The Eighth Five Year Plan blends COVID-19 recovery strategies into the macroeconomic framework and aims to implement Perspective Plan 2021-2041 so Bangladesh can reach upper-middle-income status by 2031 and eliminate extreme poverty by 2031.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct government planning document from the responsible planning body with explicit objectives and timeline.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 planning document for the target period
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: this is the government planning apparatus under Hasina's administration.
contrary_evidence: It is a plan statement, not proof of later delivery by itself.

evidence.title: From 'Digital Bangladesh' to 'Smart Bangladesh' by 2041: PM
evidence.claim: Hasina announced that her government would build Smart Bangladesh by 2041 and said the strategy rests on smart citizens, smart economy, smart government, and smart society.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report of a direct public announcement by the ruler with clear date and context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: Hasina announced the goal herself as head of government.
contrary_evidence: Announcement is not the same as economy-wide implementation.

evidence.title: Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100: Issues and Challenges of Implementation, 2022 conference page
evidence.claim: The Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100 frames a 100-year vision for a safe, climate-resilient and prosperous delta and a mission to ensure long-term water and food security, economic growth, and environmental sustainability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official planning portal summarizing the national strategy in plain language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the plan is state strategy under Hasina's government.
contrary_evidence: The page sets goals and mission, not outcomes.

evidence.title: Delta Governing Council (DGC)
evidence.claim: A Delta Governing Council chaired by the prime minister had been set up to implement the Delta Plan 2100 through policy making, strategic direction, investment planning, and Delta Fund setup.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government implementation page describing the governing body and its duties.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong: this is PM-chaired institutional machinery created under Hasina's government.
contrary_evidence: Institutional setup does not by itself prove effective execution.

evidence.title: Power Division receives 'Digital Bangladesh Award 2022'
evidence.claim: The Power Division won the Digital Bangladesh Award 2022 for ERP implementation that improved efficiency, transparency, accountability, and customer service, and the article says the system had been implemented across 15 subordinate bodies.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting with concrete implementation details and a named award.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government operational line under Hasina; the article credits agency-level execution more than personal micromanagement.
contrary_evidence: The benefits are reported by the division and the article, not independently audited in this item.

evidence.title: Learning from the education sector’s COVID-19 response to prepare for future emergencies (Bangladesh)
evidence.claim: Bangladesh's 20-month COVID-19 school closures led the Ministry of Education to create a remote learning strategy using television, radio, digital lessons, and printed materials that supported 150,933 children from marginalized groups in 842 schools.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF summary of a ministry-led response with explicit coverage figures and delivery channels.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Ministry of Education action under the Hasina government; this is not direct personal micromanagement.

chapter_notes.RECON:
Using the local prior only for structured 2022 facts, and not the client matrix, the short read is:

- In 2022, Sheikh Hasina was Bangladesh’s prime minister.
- Her formal authority was broad: the constitution places executive power in the PM’s hands and makes the PM the head of the cabinet.
- The real constraint set in 2022 was political rather than constitutional: weak checks from Parliament and the election system, restricted media space, coercive policing, and heavy institutional pressure on opposition and civil society.
- The year was shaped by inherited conditions more than by a clean policy baseline: post-2018 power concentration, entrenched corruption, Rohingya burden, pandemic aftereffects, and climate vulnerability.
- The biggest 2022 events for this ruler-period were the Padma Bridge inauguration, the northeast flood disaster, the fuel-price shock and inflation pressure, IMF stabilization talks, and the December opposition crackdown.

Retained sources, kept to the most useful cross-chapter set:

- IAEA technical / legal records: PRIS country profile, OLA safeguards listing, CNPP country profile, IAEA safety / IRRS material.

- Local and regional reporting: Prothom Alo, bdnews24, The Daily Star, The Financial Express, TBS.

- There is still no evidence that Hasina personally exercised any nuclear command authority in 2022. That is expected for Bangladesh, which is non-nuclear; more searching is unlikely to change that.

- The record on civil-nuclear safety is decent but not exhaustive.
